extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing how inventors must be named in U.S. patent applications, the required content and execution of inventor oaths/declarations (and substitute statements or assignment-statements), and procedures for correcting inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of inventor name and oath/declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent filed under section 111(a) or commencing the national stage under section 371 shall include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application. Except as otherwise provided, each individual who is the inventor or a joint inventor of a claimed invention in an application for patent shall execute an oath or declaration in connection with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline requirement: the application must identify inventors and each inventor must normally execute an oath/declaration. See related provisions for exceptions (substitute statements, assignments, earlier-filed application copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements in the oath or declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration shall contain statements that (1) the application was made or was authorized to be made by the affiant or declarant; and (2) such individual believes himself or herself to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two statements are mandatory content elements of the oath/declaration; additional statutory/ regulatory requirements may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may specify additional oath/declaration information (35 U.S.C. 115(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may specify additional information relating to the inventor and the invention that is required to be included in an oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO regulations and forms (e.g., 37 CFR, PTO forms) may require data beyond statutory minimums; consult 37 CFR 1.63 and PTO forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted substitute statement circumstances (35 U.S.C. 115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of executing an oath or declaration, the applicant may provide a substitute statement with respect to any individual who (i) is deceased; (ii) is under legal incapacity; (iii) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort; or (iv) is under an obligation to assign the invention but has refused to make the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements are limited to these permitted circumstances (and any additional circumstances the Director may specify). Use substitute statement when an inventor cannot execute the oath for these reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for substitute statements (35 U.S.C. 115(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement must (A) identify the individual with respect to whom the statement applies; (B) set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis for the filing of the substitute statement in lieu of the oath or declaration; and (C) contain any additional information, including any showing, required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute statement must explicitly explain which permitted circumstance applies and include any extra evidence or showings required by USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment may include required statements (35 U.S.C. 115(e) and 37 CFR 1.63(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual under an obligation of assignment may include the required oath/declaration statements in the assignment executed by the individual, in lieu of filing such statements separately. An assignment may serve as an oath or declaration if the assignment includes the information and statements required under 37 CFR 1.63(a) and (b) and a copy of the assignment is recorded as provided in part 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an assignment as the oath/declaration, ensure the assignment contains the same statements as an oath/declaration and is recorded appropriately; indicate dual-purpose on assignment cover sheet to alert Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing required statements (35 U.S.C. 115(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall provide each required oath or declaration, substitute statement, or recorded assignment meeting the requirements no later than the date on which the issue fee for the patent is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required statements must be on file by issue fee payment; earlier filing is typical but this sets the latest permissible date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for earlier-filed application containing required statements (35 U.S.C. 115(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements do not apply to an individual with respect to an application that claims benefit of an earlier-filed application if an oath/declaration, substitute statement, or assignment meeting requirements was executed and filed in the earlier-filed application. The Director may require copies of those documents be included in the later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on earlier-filed documents, include copies showing execution as the later application may still be required to submit them on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; savings clause (35 U.S.C. 115(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a statement may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time. Director shall establish regulations for filing additional statements if naming changes. The Director may not thereafter require additional equivalent statements once a compliant oath/declaration or assignment is filed. A patent shall not be invalid or unenforceable based on failure to comply if the failure is remedied as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is flexibility to correct or supplement statements; remedies are provided and the statute protects patents if failures are remedied per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of penalties required (35 U.S.C. 115(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed must contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 by fine or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oaths/declarations and substitute statements must include the criminal-penalty acknowledgement language.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(a) specific oath/declaration elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must: (1) Identify the inventor executing the oath by his or her legal name; (2) Identify the application to which it is directed; (3) Include a statement that the person believes the named inventor to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application; and (4) State that the application was made or was authorized to be made by the person executing the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regulatory elements implement 35 U.S.C. 115 and must appear in any oath/declaration submitted under 37 CFR 1.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(b) inventor identification and address requirement (unless ADS provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless such information is supplied in an application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76, the oath or declaration must also identify: (1) Each inventor by his or her legal name; and (2) A mailing address where the inventor customarily receives mail, and residence if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing inventor bibliographic information in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) per 1.76 (signed per 1.33(b)) obviates repeating it in the oath/declaration; unsigned ADS treated as transmittal only.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(c) competence, review, and duty to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not execute an oath or declaration unless that person has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, and is aware of the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to the person to be material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56. No minimum age, but the person must be competent to execute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the express 'reviewed and understands' wording of pre-AIA 1.63(b)(2)/(3) is not required in AIA-era filings, the declarant must still have reviewed/understood the application and be aware of duty to disclose; competence is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(d) continuing-application and copy-of-oath rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration is not required for a continuing application that claims benefit of an earlier application if an oath/declaration complying with 1.63 or a substitute statement was executed and filed in the earlier application, and a copy showing execution is submitted. The inventorship of a continuing application is specified by the ADS filed before or concurrently with the copy of the earlier oath, or by the copy itself unless accompanied by a 1.33(b) signed statement naming inventors. Any new joint inventor named must provide an oath/declaration, except as provided in 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing continuations/divisionals, rely on earlier-filed executed oaths/declarations by submitting copies that show execution; ensure new inventors provide their own oaths when added.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(e) assignment serving as oath/declaration (procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment may serve as the oath/declaration if the assignment includes the information and statements required under paragraphs (a) and (b) and a copy of the assignment is recorded as provided in part 3. Any reference to an oath or declaration includes such an assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using assignment as oath, note recordation procedures: paper assignments may be separated and forwarded for recording after application number assignment; indicate dual-purpose by check-box on assignment cover sheet; EFS-Web and EPAS have different handling (EFS-Web does not accept assignments for recording with filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(f) collective treatment for multiple inventors and substitute statements
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to an application naming more than one inventor, references to the inventor's oath or declaration mean the oaths, declarations, or substitute statements that have been collectively executed by or with respect to all joint inventors, unless otherwise clear. For single-inventor applications, substitute statement under 1.64 is treated as the oath/declaration reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All joint inventors must be covered collectively by compliant oaths/declarations/substitute statements; individual filings can be limited if ADS supplies names.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(g) execution/signature formalities and criminal-penalty acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must be executed (signed) in accordance with 37 CFR 1.66 or with an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 by fine or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both. The inventor(s) must sign unless substitute statement (signed by applicant) or assignment-statement (signed by inventor under obligation of assignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow signature rules in 1.66 (not printed here) or include the statutory penalty acknowledgement; who signs depends on the type of statement submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.63(h) placement in file record and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration filed pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 115(h)(1) will be placed in the file record of the application or patent, but may not necessarily be reviewed by the Office. Any request for correction of named inventorship must comply with 37 CFR 1.48 in an application and 37 CFR 1.324 in a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though oaths are placed in the file, examiners may not review them routinely; corrections of inventorship follow the 1.48/1.324 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of inventors when filing without ADS or oath (37 CFR 1.41(d) / pre-AIA 1.41(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: In a nonprovisional application filed without an oath/declaration or a provisional application filed without a cover sheet, the name, residence, and citizenship (or at least a name) of each person believed to be an actual inventor should be provided when application papers pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53 are filed. Where no inventor is known and applicant cannot name a person, the Office requests an alphanumeric identifier. The use of very short identifiers should be avoided to prevent confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing full identifying information at earliest opportunity helps the Office match subsequent papers to the application; failure to supply at least a unique identifier may result in resubmission of papers and loss of timely proof of earlier receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for international applications entering national stage (37 CFR 1.41(e) and 1.41(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of an international application entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 is the inventor(s) set forth in the application data sheet in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 filed with the initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371. For international design applications designating the United States, inventorship is the creator(s) set forth in the international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3). Corrections of inventorship must be pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change inventorship at national stage, file an ADS in accordance with 1.76 with the initial 371 submission; the inventor's oath/declaration cannot be used to name inventors in these cases where ADS is not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA oath/declaration requirements (applications filed before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 required execution per 1.66/1.68, identification of each inventor by full name (family name and at least one given name), country of citizenship, a statement of being the original and first inventor(s), identification of the application, review/understands clause, acknowledgement of duty to disclose under 1.56, and, unless in ADS, mailing address/residence and foreign priority applications information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA filings had more explicit 'reviewed and understands' and duty-to-disclose clauses; forms PTO/SB/01 and PTO/SB/01A were available for pre-Sept 16, 2012 filings. For continuation/divisional/CIP handling see the enumerated subparagraphs (d)/(e) in the pre-AIA section.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a new oath/declaration is required (continuations/divisionals/CIPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration is not required in a continuation/divisional if the prior application contained a compliant oath and a copy showing execution is submitted, subject to conditions (specification/drawings contain no new matter, etc.). A newly executed oath/declaration must be filed in any continuation-in-part application or in a continuation/divisional that names an inventor not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check whether the new filing adds inventors or new matter; if so, obtain newly executed oaths for added inventors and for CIPs always.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and resources for oaths/declarations (PTO forms and USPTO guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms PTO/AIA/01 through PTO/AIA/09 may be used when submitting the inventor's oath or declaration in an application filed on or after September 16, 2012. Forms PTO/SB/01 and PTO/SB/01A may be used for applications filed before September 16, 2012. AIA Inventor's Oath or Declaration Quick Reference Guide and forms are available on the USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate PTO forms and the USPTO quick reference guide to ensure compliance with formatting and required language; ADS per 37 CFR 1.76 can obviate some oath content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship procedures (37 CFR 1.48 / 35 U.S.C. 116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship in an application is permitted by amendment under 35 U.S.C. 116, implemented by 37 CFR 1.48. Requests for correction filed under 37 CFR 1.48(a) or (d) on or after September 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP; if granted, OPAP will correct Office records and send a corrected filing receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedures in 37 CFR 1.48 (and see MPEP § 602.01(c)(1) and MPEP § 602.09 for joint-inventor specifics). Correction petitions submitted on or after Sept 16, 2012 are handled administratively by OPAP regardless of original filing date.
